etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle French conférence, from Medieval Latin cōnferentia, from Latin cōnferēns.

definitions.definition: The act of consulting together formally; serious conversation or discussion; interchange of views.

quote.citation: 1599 (first performance), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Iulius Cæsar”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene ii]:
quote.text: Nor with such free and friendly conference / As he hath used of old.

quote.citation: 1850, T. S. Arthur, “Seed Time and Harvest”, in Sketches of Life and Character‎[1], Philadelphia: J. W. Bradley, →OCLC, page 129:
quote.text: Mr. Wiley, a lawyer of some ability, was sitting in his office one day, when an elderly gentleman came in and asked to have a few words of conference with him.

definitions.definition: (sciences) A formal event where scientists present their research results in speeches, workshops, posters or by other means.
(business) An event organized by a for-profit or non-profit organization to discuss a pressing issue, such as a new product, market trend or government regulation, with a range of speakers.
(sports) A group of sports teams that play each other on a regular basis.
(Philippines, sports) A constituent tournament of a sports league in a given season.
(obsolete) The act of comparing two or more things together; comparison.

quote.citation: 1594–1597, Richard Hooker, edited by J[ohn] S[penser], Of the Lawes of Ecclesiastical Politie, […], London:  […]  Will[iam] Stansby [for Matthew Lownes], published 1611, →OCLC, (please specify the page):
quote.text: helps and furtherances which  […]  the mutual conference of all men's collections and observations may afford

definitions.definition: (Methodist Church) A stated meeting of preachers and others, invested with authority to take cognizance of ecclesiastical matters.
A voluntary association of Congregational churches of a district; the district in which such churches are.
(transitive, intransitive, education) To assess (a student) by one-on-one conversation, rather than an examination.

quote.citation: 2009, Jennifer Berne, The Writing-Rich High School Classroom:
quote.text: The students who were conferenced on paper 1 will get a written response to paper 2, and those who received a written response to paper 1 will be conferenced on paper 2.
